title: Total algebra of a graded module sheaf algebra
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], P : ℕ → Mod(O_X) a family, and G a commutative unital graded sheaf algebra on P [def-weil-pbc-graded-sheaf-structures]. There exist a commutative O_X-algebra sheaf B [def-weil-pbc-comm-algebra-sheaf] and module-sheaf maps i_n : P_n → B whose cocone is a categorical coproduct [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. On every open U, for all degrees m,n and sections a,b, i_{m+n}(G.mul(a,b))=i_m(a)i_n(b); for every scalar r, i_0(G.unit(r)) is the structure-map image of r in B(U). No quasi-coherence or finiteness hypothesis is needed.

source.place: Tag 03DB, lemma-limits-colimits, sheafification of module presheaf colimits; combined with the homogeneous operations of Modules, Section 01CF.

proof.text: For each open U form the sectionwise direct sum of the P_n(U). Extend the given homogeneous bilinear multiplications by finite distributivity. The graded associativity, commutativity and unit identities make this a commutative ring, using Mathlib DirectSum.GCommRing. The scalar map r ↦ inclusion_0(G.unit(r)) is multiplicative: linearity of the unit and bilinearity reduce multiplication of scalars to the unit law. Thus this ring has the original direct-sum module scalar action. The restriction maps on each homogeneous piece extend to ring homomorphisms since G.naturality preserves multiplication and the naturality of G.unit preserves the unit. They form a presheaf of commutative algebras.

source.place: Tag 03DB, lemma-limits-colimits, sheafification of module presheaf colimits; combined with the homogeneous operations of Modules, Section 01CF.

proof.text: Sheafify this ring presheaf, and compose its structure map with the sheafification unit to obtain the algebra sheaf B. The underlying map from the direct-sum module presheaf to B is linear because the scalar map of B was defined by that composite. On underlying sections it is precisely the ring sheafification unit, which is locally injective and locally surjective. These two properties also hold for the module map: the equalizer sieves and local-image sieves are the same. This uses the Mathlib sheafification/local-bijectivity API.

source.place: Tag 03DB, lemma-limits-colimits, sheafification of module presheaf colimits; combined with the homogeneous operations of Modules, Section 01CF.

proof.text: For any module sheaf N, precomposition with this locally bijective module map gives a bijection from Hom(B,N) to Hom(the direct-sum presheaf,N). The sectionwise direct-sum universal property identifies the latter with the families of module-presheaf maps P_n→N. Since each P_n is a sheaf, these are exactly module-sheaf maps. The inverses in these two bijections provide a coproduct desc map, and their injectivity proves uniqueness. Hence the homogeneous inclusions exhibit B as the categorical module coproduct. Finally apply the ring sheafification map to the direct-sum homogeneous multiplication equation and the scalar equation to obtain the two asserted formulas.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_total {X : Scheme.{u}} (P : ℕ → X.Modules)
    (G : GradedSheafAlgebra P) :
    ∃ (B : X.CommAlgebraSheaf) (i : ∀ n, P n ⟶ B.toModule),
      Nonempty (IsColimit (Cofan.mk B.toModule i)) ∧
      (∀ (U : X.Opens) (m n : ℕ) (a : (P m).val.obj (op U))
        (b : (P n).val.obj (op U)),
        (i (m + n)).val.app (op U) (G.mul m n U a b) =
          (@id (B.right.obj.obj (op U)) ((i m).val.app (op U) a)) *
            (@id (B.right.obj.obj (op U)) ((i n).val.app (op U) b))) ∧
      (∀ (U : X.Opens) (r : Γ(X, U)),
        (i 0).val.app (op U) (G.unit.val.app (op U) r) = B.hom.hom.app (op U) r)
